decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" after "small and great" sets them side by side: they are there, the same. Death makes no difference between them.

decisions.choice: the slave is free: an owned slave released from a master
decisions.reason: The word ('eved) here means a slave owned by a master, set against "free" (chofshi), the word used for a slave's release (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12). In the grave the slave is finally set free.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Where slave and free are set against each other, "slave" is kept at every level; "servant" would lose the point (m2).

decisions.choice: slaves ... their masters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since all slaves are meant, men and women; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: "노예" at every level
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Korean uses "종" for this word, but here slave is set against free, and "노예" keeps that contrast, as the English keeps "slave" at every level.

source.text: לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Why does he give to [the] sufferer light, and life to [the] bitter of soul,

en.L: Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give light to the sufferer, \q and life to the bitter of soul,
en.B: Why is light given to those in misery, \q and life to the bitter in soul,
en.R: Why does God give light to people who suffer? \q Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give life to those whose hearts are bitter?

es.L: ¿Por qué da {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} luz al que sufre, \q y vida a los amargados de alma,
es.B: ¿Por qué se da luz a los que sufren, \q y vida a los de alma amargada,
es.R: ¿Por qué Dios da luz a los que sufren? \q ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da vida a los que tienen el corazón amargado?

fr.L: Pourquoi donne-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la lumière au malheureux, \q et la vie à ceux qui ont l’âme amère,
fr.B: Pourquoi la lumière est-elle donnée à ceux qui souffrent, \q et la vie à ceux dont l’âme est amère,
fr.R: Pourquoi Dieu donne-t-il la lumière à ceux qui souffrent ? \q Pourquoi donne-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la vie à ceux qui ont le cœur plein d’amertume ?

sw.L: Kwa nini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} humpa mwenye taabu nuru, \q na uhai wale wenye uchungu rohoni,
sw.B: Kwa nini nuru hupewa wale walio katika taabu, \q na uhai wale wenye uchungu moyoni,
sw.R: Kwa nini Mungu huwapa nuru watu wanaoteseka? \q Kwa nini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huwapa uhai wale wenye uchungu moyoni?

vi.L: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban ánh sáng cho kẻ khốn khổ, \q và sự sống cho người có linh hồn cay đắng,
vi.B: Sao ánh sáng được ban cho người khốn khổ, \q và sự sống cho kẻ có tâm hồn cay đắng,
vi.R: Sao Đức Chúa Trời lại ban ánh sáng cho người đau khổ? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban sự sống cho người có lòng cay đắng?

ko.L: 어찌하여 그분은 고난받는 자에게 빛을 주시고, \q 영혼이 쓰라린 자에게 생명을 주시는가?
ko.B: 어찌하여 고난당하는 자에게 빛이 주어지고, \q 마음이 쓰라린 자에게 생명이 주어지는가?
ko.R: 왜 하나님께서는 고통받는 사람들에게 빛을 주시는가? \q 왜 그분은 마음이 쓰라린 사람들에게 생명을 주시는가?

pt.L: Por que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dá luz ao que sofre, \q e vida aos amargurados de alma,
pt.B: Por que é dada luz aos que estão na miséria, \q e vida aos que têm a alma amargurada,
pt.R: Por que Deus dá luz a quem sofre? \q Por que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dá vida aos que têm o coração amargo?

am.L: ለጎስቋላ ብርሃንን፣ \q ነፍሳቸው ለመረረባቸውም ሕይወትን ለምን ይሰጣል?
am.B: ለጎስቋሎች ለምን ብርሃን ይሰጣል? \q ነፍሳቸው ለመረረባቸውስ ለምን ሕይወት ይሰጣል?
am.R: አምላክ ለሚሠቃዩ ሰዎች ለምን ብርሃን ይሰጣል? \q ልባቸው ለመረረባቸውስ ለምን ሕይወት ይሰጣል?

hi.L: वे दुखी को उजियाला क्यों देते हैं, \q और कड़वे मनवाले को जीवन,
hi.B: दुखी को उजियाला क्यों दिया जाता है, \q और कड़वे मनवालों को जीवन,
hi.R: परमेश्वर दुख उठानेवालों को रोशनी क्यों देते हैं? \q वे उन्हें जीवन क्यों देते हैं जिनके मन कड़वाहट से भरे हैं?

ru.L: Зачем {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} даёт страдальцу свет \q и жизнь горьким душой,
ru.B: Зачем дан свет тем, кто в беде, \q и жизнь тем, у кого горько на душе,
ru.R: Зачем Бог даёт свет тем, кто страдает? \q Зачем {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} даёт жизнь тем, у кого горечь в сердце?

ja.L: なぜ、その方は苦しむ者に光を与え、 \q 魂の苦い者に命を[与えられるのか]？
ja.B: なぜ、苦しむ者に光が与えられ、 \q 心の苦い者に命が与えられるのか？
ja.R: なぜ神は、苦しんでいる人に光を与えられるのか？ \q なぜ、心に苦しみを抱えた人に命を与えられるのか？

decisions.choice: he gives: the giver is not named, but it is God
decisions.reason: The verb is "he gives" with no subject. Job does not name God until verse 23, but he is the one who gives life and light (1:21). Literal keeps "he" and Readable names him; Balanced uses the passive, as the Hebrew leaves him unnamed.

decisions.choice: light and life: being alive
decisions.reason: "Light" stands for life itself, as in verse 16, "infants who never saw light". The two lines say the same thing twice.

decisions.choice: the bitter of soul: people in deep anguish
decisions.reason: Bitterness of soul is deep grief, as Hannah's was (1 Samuel 1:10) and that of the Shunammite whose son had died (2 Kings 4:27). The soul (nefesh) is the whole inner self.

decisions.choice: is light given
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the passive, keeping the giver unnamed as the Hebrew does (m1).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver (m1), so that the question is clear, and then uses a deity pronoun.

decisions.choice: Each Korean verse of 20-23 is a full sentence, ending in "?" or "."
alternatives: one sentence run on from verse 20 to 23
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb at the end, so a question running across four verses would leave verse 20 without its verb; each verse is closed and the next takes up the people described, keeping every verse's content after its own marker.

decisions.choice: Verses 20-23 are one question at Literal: verse 20 asks it, verses 21-23 add, in phrases with "ለ..." ("to those who ..."), the people it is asked about.
alternatives: a full question in every verse
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb at the end, so the Hebrew's single question is kept by asking it once and letting the "to ..." phrases follow; Balanced keeps the same chain after a full question in verse 20, and Readable gives each verse its own sentence, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: honorific "वे" for the unnamed giver; no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The English marks the unnamed giver as God with a deity pronoun (meaning m1). Hindi has no capital letters; the honorific plural "वे ... देते हैं" shows respect, Balanced keeps the passive as the English does, and Readable names God. This holds for the whole file.

decisions.choice: The one long question of 3:20-23 is split: 3:20 and 3:23 ask "why", and 3:21-22 describe the sufferers in sentences of their own ("彼らは…").
alternatives: one Japanese sentence over four verses
decisions.reason: Japanese relative clauses come before their noun; separate sentences keep each verse's content after its own number. God, unnamed in the Hebrew, is "その方" (L) as in David's song.

source.text: הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: those who wait for death, and it [is] not, and they dig for it more than [for] hidden treasures,

en.L: who wait for death, and it [does] not [come], \q and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
en.B: who long for death, but it does not come, \q and search for it more than for hidden treasure,
en.R: They long for death, but it does not come. \q They search for it harder than people dig for buried treasure.

es.L: que esperan la muerte, y no [llega], \q y cavan por ella más que por tesoros escondidos,
es.B: que anhelan la muerte, pero no llega, \q y la buscan más que a un tesoro escondido,
es.R: Desean la muerte, pero no llega. \q La buscan con más empeño que quien cava buscando un tesoro enterrado.

fr.L: qui attendent la mort, et elle [ne vient] pas, \q et la cherchent en creusant plus que des trésors cachés,
fr.B: qui aspirent à la mort, mais elle ne vient pas, \q et qui la recherchent plus qu’un trésor caché,
fr.R: Ils désirent la mort, mais elle ne vient pas. \q Ils la cherchent plus ardemment que ceux qui creusent pour trouver un trésor enfoui.

sw.L: wanaongojea kifo, nacho [hakiji], \q na kukichimbua kuliko hazina zilizofichwa,
sw.B: wanaotamani kifo lakini hakiji, \q na kukitafuta kuliko hazina iliyofichwa,
sw.R: Wanatamani kufa, lakini kifo hakiji. \q Wanakitafuta kwa bidii kuliko watu wanaochimba kutafuta hazina iliyofichwa.

vi.L: là những kẻ trông chờ sự chết, mà nó [chẳng đến], \q và đào tìm nó hơn tìm kho báu giấu kín,
vi.B: là những người mong chết mà cái chết chẳng đến, \q và tìm kiếm nó hơn tìm kho báu chôn giấu,
vi.R: Họ mong được chết, nhưng cái chết không đến. \q Họ tìm cái chết còn hơn người ta đào bới tìm kho báu.

ko.L: 그들은 죽음을 기다려도 [오지] 않고, \q 숨겨진 보물보다 더 그것을 파서 찾는다.
ko.B: 그들은 죽기를 바라도 죽음이 오지 않아, \q 숨겨진 보물을 찾기보다 더 애써 죽음을 찾는다.
ko.R: 그들은 죽기를 바라지만 죽음은 오지 않는다. \q 그들은 땅에 묻힌 보물을 찾는 사람보다 더 열심히 죽음을 찾는다.

pt.L: que esperam pela morte, e ela não [vem], \q e cavam por ela mais do que por tesouros escondidos,
pt.B: que anseiam pela morte, mas ela não vem, \q e a procuram mais do que a um tesouro escondido,
pt.R: Eles desejam a morte, mas ela não vem. \q Procuram por ela com mais esforço do que quem cava atrás de um tesouro enterrado.

am.L: ሞትን ለሚጠባበቁ፣ እርሱ ግን ለሌለ፣ \q ከተሸሸገ ሀብት ይልቅ ለሚቆፍሩለት፣
am.B: ሞትን ለሚናፍቁ፣ እርሱ ግን ለማይመጣላቸው፣ \q ከተቀበረ ሀብት ይልቅ ለሚፈልጉት፣
am.R: ሞትን ይናፍቃሉ፤ እርሱ ግን አይመጣም። \q ሰዎች የተቀበረ ሀብት ከሚቆፍሩት በላይ ሞትን አጥብቀው ይፈልጋሉ።

hi.L: जो मृत्यु की बाट जोहते हैं, और वह [आती] नहीं, \q और गड़े हुए धन से बढ़कर उसे खोदकर ढूँढते हैं,
hi.B: जो मृत्यु की लालसा करते हैं, पर वह नहीं आती, \q और छिपे ख़ज़ाने से भी बढ़कर उसे ढूँढते हैं,
hi.R: वे मृत्यु के लिए तरसते हैं, पर वह नहीं आती। \q वे उसे उससे भी ज़्यादा मेहनत से ढूँढते हैं जितना लोग गड़ा हुआ ख़ज़ाना खोदते हैं।

ru.L: которые ждут смерти, а её нет, \q и роют [в поисках] её больше, чем [в поисках] скрытых сокровищ,
ru.B: тем, кто ждёт смерти, но она не приходит, \q кто ищет её больше, чем спрятанное сокровище,
ru.R: Они ждут смерти, но она не приходит. \q Они ищут её усерднее, чем люди копают в поисках зарытого клада.

ja.L: 彼らは死を待つが、それは[来]ない。 \q 隠された宝よりも[熱心に]それを掘り求める。
ja.B: 彼らは死を待ち焦がれるが、死は来ない。 \q 隠された宝を探すよりも熱心に、死を探し求める。
ja.R: 彼らは死を待ちこがれているのに、死はやって来ない。 \q 埋められた宝を掘るよりも熱心に、死を探している。

decisions.choice: wait for: long for, wait eagerly
decisions.reason: The verb (chakah) is used of waiting with longing (Isaiah 30:18; Psalm 33:20). These people long for death as others long for good things.

decisions.choice: dig for it more than for hidden treasure: seek it with all their effort
decisions.reason: Buried treasure was sought with great effort (Proverbs 2:4; compare Job 28:1-11). Those in misery search for death harder than anyone digs for gold.

decisions.choice: [does] not [come]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "and it is not"; Literal supplies the verb in brackets.

source.text: הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי־גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ־קָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: the [ones] rejoicing to rejoicing; they exult when they find [the] grave,

en.L: who rejoice to [the point of] gladness, \q [who] exult when they find the grave,
en.B: who are filled with joy \q and glad when they find the grave,
en.R: They are full of joy \q when at last they find the grave.

es.L: que se alegran hasta [el] regocijo, \q [que] se gozan cuando hallan el sepulcro,
es.B: que se llenan de alegría \q y se gozan cuando encuentran el sepulcro,
es.R: Se llenan de alegría \q cuando por fin encuentran la tumba.

fr.L: qui se réjouissent jusqu’[à] l’allégresse, \q [qui] exultent quand ils trouvent le tombeau,
fr.B: qui sont remplis de joie \q et heureux quand ils trouvent le tombeau,
fr.R: Ils sont pleins de joie \q quand enfin ils trouvent le tombeau.

sw.L: wanaofurahi hata [kufikia] shangwe, \q [wanaoshangilia] wanapolipata kaburi,
sw.B: wanaojaa furaha \q na kushangilia wanapolipata kaburi,
sw.R: Wanajaa furaha \q wanapolipata kaburi hatimaye.

vi.L: là những kẻ vui mừng đến [độ] hân hoan, \q [và] hớn hở khi tìm được mồ mả,
vi.B: là những người tràn đầy niềm vui \q và hớn hở khi tìm được mồ mả,
vi.R: Họ vô cùng vui sướng \q khi cuối cùng tìm được mồ mả.

ko.L: 그들은 기뻐 뛰놀 만큼 즐거워하고, \q 무덤을 찾으면 크게 기뻐한다.
ko.B: 그들은 기쁨에 넘쳐서, \q 무덤을 찾으면 즐거워한다.
ko.R: 그들은 마침내 무덤을 찾게 되면 \q 기뻐서 어쩔 줄 모른다.

pt.L: que se alegram até o júbilo, \q [que] exultam quando acham a sepultura,
pt.B: que se enchem de alegria \q e ficam felizes quando encontram a sepultura,
pt.R: Eles ficam cheios de alegria \q quando finalmente encontram a sepultura.

am.L: እስከ ሐሤት ድረስ ደስ ለሚላቸው፣ \q መቃብርን ባገኙ ጊዜ ሐሤት ለሚያደርጉ፣
am.B: በደስታ ለሚሞሉ፣ \q መቃብርን ሲያገኙ ሐሤት ለሚያደርጉ፣
am.R: እጅግ ደስ ይላቸዋል፤ \q በመጨረሻ መቃብርን ሲያገኙ።

hi.L: जो अत्यंत आनंद [तक] आनंदित होते हैं, \q [और] जब क़ब्र पाते हैं, तो मगन होते हैं,
hi.B: जो आनंद से भर जाते हैं \q और क़ब्र पाकर मगन होते हैं,
hi.R: वे आनंद से भर जाते हैं \q जब आख़िरकार उन्हें क़ब्र मिल जाती है।

ru.L: которые радуются до ликования, \q веселятся, когда находят могилу,
ru.B: кто переполнен радостью \q и ликует, когда находит могилу,
ru.R: Они полны радости, \q когда наконец находят могилу.

ja.L: 彼らは喜びに至るまで喜び、 \q 墓を見いだすと、小躍りする。
ja.B: 彼らは喜びにあふれ、 \q 墓を見つけると、大喜びする。
ja.R: やっと墓を見つけると、 \q 彼らは喜びでいっぱいになる。

decisions.choice: rejoicing to rejoicing: joy beyond measure
decisions.reason: "Rejoicing to rejoicing" builds the word on itself for emphasis: they are glad to the point of exultation. Some read the last word as gal, "heap" (of stones over a grave), with different vowels, which would fit "the grave" in the next line; the Hebrew as it is pointed reads "rejoicing".

decisions.choice: when they find the grave: the end of their search
decisions.reason: The word "find" completes the picture of verse 21: those who dig for death as for treasure are glad when at last they find it.

source.text: לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר־דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: to a man whose way is hidden, and [whom] has hedged God around him?

en.L: to a man whose way is hidden, \q and whom God has hedged in?
en.B: to a man whose way is hidden from him, \q whom God has fenced in?
en.R: Why give life to a man who cannot see where his life is going, \q whom God has shut in on every side?

es.L: al hombre cuyo camino está escondido, \q y a quien Dios ha cercado?
es.B: al hombre cuyo camino le está oculto, \q a quien Dios ha encerrado con un cerco?
es.R: ¿Por qué dar vida a un hombre que no ve hacia dónde va su vida, \q a quien Dios ha encerrado por todos lados?

fr.L: à l’homme dont le chemin est caché, \q et que Dieu a entouré d’une haie ?
fr.B: à l’homme dont le chemin lui est caché, \q que Dieu a enfermé derrière une haie ?
fr.R: Pourquoi donner la vie à un homme qui ne voit pas où va sa vie, \q que Dieu a enfermé de tous côtés ?

sw.L: kwa mtu ambaye njia yake imefichwa, \q na ambaye Mungu amemzungushia uzio?
sw.B: kwa mtu ambaye njia yake imefichika kwake, \q ambaye Mungu amemzungushia uzio?
sw.R: Kwa nini ampe uhai mtu asiyeona maisha yake yanaelekea wapi, \q ambaye Mungu amemfungia pande zote?

vi.L: cho người có đường lối bị che khuất, \q và bị Đức Chúa Trời rào quanh?
vi.B: cho người không thấy được đường lối mình, \q người mà Đức Chúa Trời đã rào kín?
vi.R: Sao lại ban sự sống cho người không thấy đời mình đi về đâu, \q người bị Đức Chúa Trời vây kín mọi bề?

ko.L: 길이 숨겨진 사람에게, \q 하나님께서 사방을 울타리로 막으신 사람에게 어찌하여 [생명을 주시는가]?
ko.B: 자기 앞길이 보이지 않는 사람, \q 하나님께서 울타리로 가두신 사람에게 어찌하여 생명을 주시는가?
ko.R: 왜 하나님께서는 자기 인생이 어디로 가는지 모르는 사람에게 생명을 주시는가? \q 왜 사방을 막아 가두신 사람에게 생명을 주시는가?

pt.L: a um homem cujo caminho está escondido, \q e a quem Deus cercou?
pt.B: a um homem cujo caminho lhe está escondido, \q a quem Deus cercou por todos os lados?
pt.R: Por que dar vida a um homem que não consegue ver para onde vai a sua vida, \q a quem Deus fechou por todos os lados?

am.L: መንገዱ ለተሰወረበት ሰው፣ \q አምላክም ዙሪያውን ላጠረበት?
am.B: መንገዱ ለተሰወረበት ሰው፣ \q አምላክ በዙሪያው አጥር ለሠራበት?
am.R: ሕይወቱ ወዴት እንደሚሄድ ለማያይ ሰው ለምን ሕይወት ይሰጣል? \q አምላክ በዙሪያው አጥሮ ለዘጋበት ሰው?

hi.L: उस पुरुष को, जिसका मार्ग छिपा है, \q और जिसे परमेश्वर ने घेर लिया है?
hi.B: उस पुरुष को, जिससे उसका मार्ग छिपा है, \q जिसे परमेश्वर ने घेरकर बंद कर दिया है?
hi.R: ऐसे मनुष्य को जीवन क्यों दिया जाए जो देख नहीं सकता कि उसका जीवन किधर जा रहा है, \q जिसे परमेश्वर ने हर ओर से घेरकर बंद कर दिया है?

ru.L: человеку, чей путь сокрыт, \q и которого Бог оградил?
ru.B: человеку, чей путь от него сокрыт, \q кого Бог обнёс оградой?
ru.R: Зачем давать жизнь человеку, который не видит, куда идёт его жизнь, \q кого Бог запер со всех сторон?

ja.L: 自分の道が隠され、 \q 神が囲いを巡らされた人に、[なぜ光が与えられるのか]？
ja.B: なぜ、自分の行く道が隠され、 \q 神が周りに垣を巡らされた人に、命が与えられるのか？
ja.R: 自分の人生がどこへ向かうのかもわからず、 \q 神に四方を閉じ込められた人に、なぜ命を与えられるのか？

decisions.choice: God has hedged him in: the hedge of 1:10, now felt as a prison
decisions.reason: The verb (sukh) is the one the Accuser used in 1:10: "Have you not put a hedge around him?" There the hedge was God's protection. Job now feels God's hedge as a wall that shuts him in with no way out (19:8).

decisions.choice: whose way is hidden: who cannot see where his life is going or why
decisions.reason: A person's way is the course of his life. Job cannot see the reason for what has happened or any way forward.

decisions.choice: to a man: Job speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The question that began in verse 20 ("why is light given ...") ends here. Job speaks of anyone in misery, but verses 24-26 show that he means himself; "a man" (gever) is the word used of him in verse 3. So no inclusive wording is used.

decisions.choice: Why give life to
decisions.reason: Readable broke verses 20-22 into short sentences, so it repeats the question here.

decisions.choice: hidden from him
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "from him" so that "hidden" is understood as he cannot see it (m2).

decisions.choice: "cercado"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word of 1:10 ("un cerco alrededor de él"), so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "entouré d'une haie" (L), "enfermé derrière une haie" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "haie" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "amemzungushia uzio" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "uzio" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "rào quanh" (L), "rào kín" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the verb "rào" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "울타리로 막으신" (L), "울타리로 가두신" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "울타리" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Deus cercou
decisions.reason: "Cercar" is the verb of the hedge in 1:10 ("puseste uma cerca ao redor dele"), so Portuguese keeps the echo m1 describes: the protection is now felt as a wall.

decisions.choice: "घेर लिया" (Literal); "घेरकर बंद कर दिया" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the protecting hedge in 1:10 (meaning m1), where Hindi says "घेरा"; keeping the same root lets the reader hear that the protection is now felt as a prison.

decisions.choice: оградил (L); обнёс оградой (B)
decisions.reason: The verb recalls the hedge of 1:10 (m1), now felt as a prison; Literal and Balanced use the words of 1:10 ("оградил", "ограду") so the echo is heard. Readable says "запер", as the English Readable says "shut in".

decisions.choice: vayasekh "囲いを巡らされた" (L), "垣を巡らされた" (B), echoing "垣を巡らされた" of 1:10 (m1).
decisions.reason: Keeps the link the meaning decision points to: the hedge of protection is now a prison.

source.text: כִּֽי־לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For before my bread my sighing comes, and pour out like water my groans.

en.L: For before my bread my sighing comes, \q and my groans pour out like water.
en.B: For sighing comes to me in place of food, \q and my groans pour out like water.
en.R: Instead of food, I have sighing. \q My groans pour out like water.

es.L: Porque delante de mi pan llega mi suspiro, \q y como agua se derraman mis gemidos.
es.B: Porque los suspiros me llegan en lugar de comida, \q y mis gemidos se derraman como el agua.
es.R: En vez de comida, tengo suspiros. \q Mis gemidos corren como el agua.

fr.L: Car avant mon pain vient mon soupir, \q et mes gémissements se répandent comme l’eau.
fr.B: Car les soupirs me tiennent lieu de nourriture, \q et mes plaintes déferlent comme l’eau.
fr.R: Au lieu de manger, je soupire. \q Mes gémissements coulent comme de l’eau.

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla ya mkate wangu kuugua kwangu huja, \q na kilio changu chamwagika kama maji.
sw.B: Kwa maana kuugua kunanijia badala ya chakula, \q na kilio changu kinamiminika kama maji.
sw.R: Badala ya chakula, nina kuugua. \q Kilio changu kinamwagika kama maji.

vi.L: Vì trước bánh tôi, tiếng thở than tôi đến, \q và tiếng rên rỉ tôi tuôn ra như nước.
vi.B: Vì tiếng thở than thay cho đồ ăn của tôi, \q và tiếng rên rỉ tôi tuôn trào như nước.
vi.R: Thay vì ăn, tôi chỉ thở than. \q Tiếng rên rỉ của tôi tuôn ra như nước.

ko.L: 내 빵 앞에 내 탄식이 오고, \q 내 신음은 물처럼 쏟아진다.
ko.B: 한숨이 밥 대신 나를 찾아오고, \q 신음이 물처럼 쏟아진다.
ko.R: 나는 먹는 대신 한숨만 쉰다. \q 내 신음 소리가 물처럼 쏟아진다.

pt.L: Pois antes do meu pão vem o meu suspiro, \q e os meus gemidos se derramam como água.
pt.B: Pois os suspiros me vêm no lugar da comida, \q e os meus gemidos se derramam como água.
pt.R: Em vez de comida, eu tenho suspiros. \q Os meus gemidos se derramam como água.

am.L: ከእንጀራዬ በፊት ማቃሰቴ ይመጣልና፤ \q ጩኸቴም እንደ ውኃ ይፈስሳል።
am.B: ከምግብ ይልቅ ማቃሰት ይመጣብኛልና፤ \q ጩኸቴም እንደ ውኃ ይፈስሳል።
am.R: ከምግብ ይልቅ ማቃሰት ሆኖልኛል። \q ጩኸቴ እንደ ውኃ ይፈስሳል።

hi.L: क्योंकि मेरी रोटी से पहले मेरी आहें आती हैं, \q और मेरी कराहें पानी के समान उमड़ पड़ती हैं।
hi.B: क्योंकि भोजन के बदले मुझे आहें मिलती हैं, \q और मेरी कराहें पानी के समान उमड़ पड़ती हैं।
hi.R: भोजन के बदले मेरे पास बस आहें हैं। \q मेरी कराहें पानी की तरह बहती हैं।

ru.L: Ведь прежде хлеба моего приходит вздох мой, \q и льются, как вода, стоны мои.
ru.B: Ведь вместо пищи мне — вздохи, \q и стоны мои льются, как вода.
ru.R: Вместо еды у меня — вздохи. \q Мои стоны льются, как вода.

ja.L: まことに、わたしのパンの前に、わたしのため息が来る。 \q わたしのうめきは水のように注ぎ出る。
ja.B: 食べ物の代わりに、ため息がわたしに来る。 \q わたしのうめきは水のようにあふれ出る。
ja.R: 食べ物の代わりに、わたしにはため息しかない。 \q うめき声が、水のようにあふれ出る。

decisions.choice: before my bread: in place of food, as my daily food
decisions.reason: "Before my bread" can mean that sighing comes ahead of his food, or in place of it, as in "my tears have been my food day and night" (Psalm 42:4). Either way, grief fills his days.

decisions.choice: my groans: loud cries of pain
decisions.reason: The word (she'agah) is used of a lion's roar (4:10). Job's cries of pain are loud and pour out without stopping.

decisions.choice: in place of food (B); instead of food (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the more likely sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps it as it is.

source.text: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד פָּ֭חַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵ֑נִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָ֝גֹ֗רְתִּי יָ֣בֹא לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For a fear I feared, and it came to me, and what I dreaded, it came to me.

en.L: For a fear I feared, and it has come upon me; \q and what I dreaded has come to me.
en.B: For the thing I feared has come upon me, \q and what I dreaded has happened to me.
en.R: The thing I was afraid of has happened to me. \q What I dreaded has come true.

es.L: Porque un temor temí, y ha venido sobre mí; \q y lo que yo temía me ha llegado.
es.B: Porque lo que temía ha caído sobre mí, \q y lo que me aterraba me ha sucedido.
es.R: Lo que me daba miedo me ha pasado. \q Lo que yo temía se ha hecho realidad.

fr.L: Car une crainte, je l’ai crainte, et elle est venue sur moi ; \q et ce que je redoutais m’est arrivé.
fr.B: Car ce que je craignais m’est tombé dessus, \q et ce que je redoutais m’est arrivé.
fr.R: Ce dont j’avais peur m’est arrivé. \q Ce que je redoutais est devenu réalité.

sw.L: Kwa maana hofu niliyoiogopa imenijia, \q na lile nililoliogopa limenifikia.
sw.B: Kwa maana jambo nililoliogopa limenipata, \q na lile lililonitisha limenitokea.
sw.R: Kile nilichokuwa nikiogopa kimenipata. \q Kile nilichohofia kimetimia.

vi.L: Vì một nỗi sợ tôi đã sợ, và nó đã đến trên tôi; \q và điều tôi kinh hãi đã đến với tôi.
vi.B: Vì điều tôi sợ đã giáng xuống trên tôi, \q và điều tôi kinh hãi đã xảy đến cho tôi.
vi.R: Điều tôi sợ đã xảy ra với tôi. \q Điều tôi lo lắng đã thành sự thật.

ko.L: 내가 두려워한 두려움, 그것이 내게 닥쳤고, \q 내가 무서워하던 것이 내게 왔다.
ko.B: 내가 두려워하던 일이 내게 닥쳤고, \q 내가 무서워하던 일이 내게 일어났다.
ko.R: 내가 겁내던 일이 나에게 일어났다. \q 내가 걱정하던 일이 현실이 되었다.

pt.L: Pois um temor eu temi, e ele veio sobre mim; \q e o que eu receava chegou até mim.
pt.B: Pois caiu sobre mim aquilo que eu temia, \q e aconteceu comigo o que me dava pavor.
pt.R: Aconteceu comigo aquilo de que eu tinha medo. \q O que eu temia virou realidade.

am.L: የፈራሁት ፍርሃት መጥቶብኛልና፤ \q የሰጋሁትም ደርሶብኛል።
am.B: የፈራሁት ነገር መጥቶብኛልና፤ \q የሰጋሁትም ደርሶብኛል።
am.R: የፈራሁት ነገር ደርሶብኛል። \q የሰጋሁት ነገር ተፈጽሟል።

hi.L: क्योंकि मैं एक भय से डरा, और वह मुझ पर आ पड़ा है; \q और जिससे मैं घबराता था, वह मुझ पर आ गया है।
hi.B: क्योंकि जिस बात से मैं डरता था, वही मुझ पर आ पड़ी है, \q और जिससे मैं घबराता था, वही मेरे साथ हुआ है।
hi.R: जिस बात से मैं डरता था, वही मेरे साथ हो गई है। \q जिससे मैं घबराता था, वह सच हो गया है।

ru.L: Ведь страх, которого я страшился, пришёл ко мне, \q и чего я боялся, то пришло ко мне.
ru.B: Ведь то, чего я страшился, обрушилось на меня, \q и чего я боялся, то со мной случилось.
ru.R: То, чего я боялся, случилось со мной. \q Чего я страшился, то сбылось.

decisions.choice: a fear I feared: the thing I greatly feared
decisions.reason: The noun and verb from the same root (pachad) make a strong phrase: the very thing he feared.

decisions.choice: it has come: what he once feared has now happened
alternatives: whatever I fear comes upon me (each new fear)
decisions.reason: The verbs point to the past: what Job feared before has come. They could also mean that each thing he fears comes true. The prologue shows a man careful against disaster, offering sacrifices in case his children had sinned (1:5); the text does not say more about what he feared.

decisions.choice: the thing I feared
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the doubled word (m1) in plain English.

ja.B: わたしには安らぎも、静けさも、休みもない。 \q ただ混乱が来るだけだ。
ja.R: わたしには、平安も、静けさも、休みもない。 \q あるのは苦しみだけだ。

decisions.choice: quiet, rest, turmoil: what the dead have and Job does not
decisions.reason: Job has none of what he said the grave would give: quiet (verse 13) and rest (verses 13, 17). And the turmoil (rogez) that the wicked lay aside in death (verse 17) has come on him. The chapter ends on that word.

decisions.choice: I am not ... turmoil comes: his state now
decisions.reason: The verbs describe the state Job is in as he speaks, so they are rendered in the present.

decisions.choice: only turmoil comes
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "only" where the Hebrew has "and", since the turmoil is all that comes in place of the rest he lacks.
